comparator.name: Bachelor Informatiekunde (Information Science)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 official guide has 55 EC of compulsory propedeutic courses and 65 EC of fixed postpropedeutic work including 10 EC of research methods and a 5-EC pre-thesis course. It also requires 15 EC selected from six restricted Analytics/Innovation courses, 30 EC of genuine free elective space, and a 15-EC final project: 180 EC. The chosen restricted courses are Python programming, Big Data for Dynamic Systems and Innovation Management. They represent computing, analytics and organisational innovation without treating either Analytics or Innovation as a formal route. The standard 10-EC methods course is selected, rather than its intensive summer version.

alternatives.concept: Combines programming, databases, data analysis and system design with organisational change, user needs, research methods, security and responsible technology. It follows OU Informatiekunde’s bridge between computing and management while acknowledging that UCR lacks its formal enterprise-modelling, ontology, project-management and compulsory information-science research sequence.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the broad route, this curriculum replaces four courses focused on product design, organisational leadership, communication and digital transformation with linear algebra, numerical methods, linear systems and advanced statistics. These are genuine consequences of the official Analytics direction and meet the pairwise 30-EC floor.

alternatives.concept: Develops OU Informatiekunde’s Programming and Technology learning line through programming, databases, networks and operating systems, software development, algorithms, discrete mathematics and selected AI methods. It is a technical direction within information science, not a claim to reproduce the OU programme’s organisational and management core.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match covers the overall OU bridge between information systems, organisations, data, programming, security and research. Its formal data-and-information-management learning line and Analytics choice support a more quantitative second route. The separate Programming and Technology line supports a technical software-and-systems third route. The remaining generator-eligible interests are substantively represented in the closest match; all three feasible curricula have distinct organising priorities and pass pairwise 30-EC differences.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Introduction to Programming provides computing foundations but does not reproduce the whole OU introductory survey.
Logic & Discrete Mathematics directly addresses formal reasoning and discrete structures.
Software Development overlaps with implementation practice but does not reproduce the object-oriented programming course.
OU requires a dedicated software-engineering course; UCR has software-development study but it is already displayed against programming.
OU selects Python programming within the restricted choice; UCR programming appears elsewhere and is not repeated.
UCR lacks a dedicated enterprise-modelling course.
The OU introductory course surveys the information-science field; the UCR curriculum introduces its strands across several courses.
Database Systems directly addresses relational database design and querying.
Audience-aware communication overlaps with professional communication but differs in scope and practice format.
Responsible AI examines privacy and digital risks, but does not reproduce OU’s socio-technical information-security course.
Product design develops user-needs analysis and prototyping but does not reproduce formal object-oriented analysis.
UCR lacks a dedicated ontology-engineering course.
Data Science introduces analysis and visualisation but not the full OU business-analytics course.
Probability & Statistics addresses quantitative inference, though with different mathematical scope.
Machine Learning addresses data-intensive analysis but not the specific R-based dynamic-systems course.
Research Methods & Statistics addresses research design and empirical analysis, without reproducing OU’s 10-EC information-science methods course.
AI in the Economy examines organisational and societal consequences of AI, with a different disciplinary emphasis.
Organizational Psychology addresses behaviour and change in organisations.
OU requires Management accounting; UCR business courses in these routes do not reproduce it.
Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations addresses organisational design and strategy, with different scope.
Strategy & Digital Transformation addresses technology implementation but not OU’s dedicated project-management methods.
Ethics examines normative questions relevant to digital innovation, but is broader than OU’s specialist course.
AI in the Economy examines strategic implications of digital technology, but not the full information-management curriculum.
Strategy & Digital Transformation addresses innovation in organisations, with different scope.
Personal & Professional Development supports academic formation but is not the same as OU’s information-science skills course.
OU requires formal preparation for its supervised final project; UCR has no equivalent scheduled course.
OU reserves 30 EC for genuine approved elective space.
OU requires a 15-EC information-science thesis. UCR optional independent research appears separately in the comparison.

notes.text: OU Informatiekunde has dedicated enterprise modelling, ontology engineering, socio-technical security, management accounting, project management, a compulsory 10-EC information-science methods course and a 15-EC final project. UCR offers related systems, data and organisational courses, but its three pathways do not reproduce that full specialist sequence. OU also has 15 EC of restricted Analytics/Innovation choice and 30 EC of genuine open elective space.
